The paper addresses the gap that current path planning methods do not consider aircraft pose uncertainty when calculating probability of detection.
Aircraft pose uncertainty arises from two sources: physical limitations/environmental factors (e.g., wind) and inertial navigation system estimation errors.
The probability of detection is a nonlinear function of aircraft pose, radar position, and aircraft physical characteristics like radar cross section.
North's approximation for probability of detection is used: P_D ≈ 0.5 × erfc(√(-ln(P_fa) - √S + 0.5)).
The signal-to-noise ratio is expressed as S = (c_r × σ_r) / (k × R^4), where both σ_r and R depend on aircraft pose.
The constant RCS model is the simplest, with σ_rc = c_c, independent of aircraft pose.
The ellipsoid RCS model is a 3D surface given by σ_re = (π(abc)²) / ((a×sin(λ)×cos(φ))² + (b×sin(λ)×sin(φ))² + (c×cos(λ))²).
The simple spikeball RCS model has the form σ_rs = |a_s × sin(n × λ)| + b_s, where n determines the number of lobes.
The linearization uses a first-order Taylor series expansion about a nominal aircraft state to approximate variations in P_D.
The variance of P_D is computed using the similarity transform: C_PD = A_P × C_xx × A_P^T.
The Jacobian matrix A_P combines five partial derivatives: ∂P_D/∂S, ∂S/∂R, ∂R/∂x_a, ∂S/∂σ_r, and ∂σ_r/∂x_a.
The validation experiments used a nominal range of 650 km, which ensures P_D is near 0.5 for some azimuth angles.
1000 Monte Carlo runs were performed with aircraft azimuth angles from 0 to 180 degrees in 0.5-degree increments.
For the constant RCS model, P_D variability was less than 0.1% with medium aircraft state uncertainty.
For the ellipsoid RCS model, P_D ranged from near 0 to 0.7 as a function of radar azimuth angle.
The spikeball RCS model showed biased Monte Carlo ensembles at azimuth angles of 0, 90, and 180 degrees due to sharp corners.
The 3-σ_pd bounds from the linearized model appropriately bounded Monte Carlo results for all three RCS models.
Low uncertainty level: 0.1 m position standard deviation and 0.1° Euler angle standard deviation.
Medium uncertainty level: 10 m position standard deviation and 1° Euler angle standard deviation.
High uncertainty level: 100 m position standard deviation and 2° Euler angle standard deviation.
The radar constant c_r used in experiments was 167.4 J·m²/°K.
The probability of false alarm P_fa was set to 1.7e-4 in the validation experiments.
The aircraft position is represented in the NED (North-East-Down) coordinate frame.
The aircraft orientation is represented using Euler angles: roll (φ_a), pitch (θ_a), and yaw (ψ_a).
The direction cosine matrix R_nb is formed using the ZYX Euler angle sequence to transform between NED and body frames.
